title: Six AI-proof skills: agents, distribution, robotics, curation, builder-distributor, IRL community
summary: Greg lays out six skill sets that gain value as AI improves, each with a concrete first rep. The throughline: building is getting cheap, so attention, trust, taste and real-world belonging become the scarce assets, and the winners combine several skills.

principles.text: When anyone can ship a product with AI, the bottleneck moves from building to making people care, so distribution is the scarce skill.
principles.quote: when anyone can ship a landing page or an app, you know, or build a SaaS, uh the bottle the bottleneck moves to the question of can you make people care?

principles.text: Start distribution by asking what existing desire you are pointing the product at before building it, not after it is done.
principles.quote: you want to start asking yourself, "What existing desire am I pointing this at?" before you built.

principles.text: Learn to build agents by shipping one small, scheduled agent with a clear success metric, not a giant all-knowing one.
principles.quote: The better move is basically just to build small agent to start, get it to be very valuable, schedule it, have a clear success metric

principles.text: Build-and-distribute in one loop: make the smallest AI-built version, then create 10 pieces of distribution within 48 hours, before you feel ready.
principles.quote: Then create 10 pieces of distribution for it before you even feel ready.

principles.text: Curation wins when it carries a take; with AI slop flooding feeds, raw authentic yapping is what algorithms are promoting.
principles.quote: That structure forces you to have a take, which is the difference between curation and forwarding links.

principles.text: As AI makes content, software and advice abundant, scarcity shifts to belonging, trust and context; small bespoke IRL rooms turned into networks via recaps capture it.
principles.quote: scarcity moves towards belonging, trust, and contexts.
